summary: Slow query execution with RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE waits due to memory pressure and parallelism.
symptoms: RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE waits observed during high user connection counts.
Slow query execution exacerbated by parallel query execution.
mechanism: RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE waits occur when queries request memory grants that exceed available resources, often exacerbated by parallelism and high concurrency.

facts.evidence: Post mentions RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE waits during sp_whoisactive.

facts.key: Parallel query execution contributing to waits
facts.evidence: Post mentions CXCONSUMER waits and MAXDOP set to 0.
Post mentions forced grants in sys.dm_exec_query_resource_semaphores.

assumptions: Parallelism is a significant contributor to RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE waits.
Memory pressure is caused by high concurrency and large memory grants.
unknowns: Exact workload characteristics causing memory pressure.
Impact of NUMA configuration on memory grants and waits.
